brief: A 3D-printed PLA stepper-motor mounting plate, 120 mm long, 80 mm wide and 8 mm thick, with all four corners rounded to a 10 mm radius and a 1 mm chamfer round its top edge. On top, in the centre of the plate, a cylindrical boss 36 mm in diameter standing 6 mm proud of the plate, blended into it with a 2 mm fillet, so the part is 14 mm tall overall. A 22.5 mm bore through the boss and the plate, in the centre. Four 3.4 mm holes on a 31 mm square of centres, centred on the plate, for the motor. Six 4.5 mm holes equally spaced on a 56 mm bolt circle, centred on the plate. Four 5.5 mm corner holes on a 104 x 64 mm rectangle of centres, centred on the plate, each counterbored 10 mm in diameter and 4 mm deep from the top. Two 20 x 5 mm slots running along the plate's length, centred across the width, with their centres 14 mm from each end. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: A flat plate intended to mount a stepper motor via a bolt pattern and central bore, itself fixed down through a set of corner and bolt-circle holes, printed in PLA.

All four corners rounded to 10 mm radius
1 mm chamfer around the top edge
Cylindrical boss on top, centred, 36 mm diameter, 6 mm proud of plate, blended with 2 mm fillet
Overall part height 14 mm (8 mm plate + 6 mm boss)
22.5 mm bore through boss and plate, centred
Four 3.4 mm holes on a 31 mm square of centres, centred on the plate (motor fixing holes)
Six 4.5 mm holes equally spaced on a 56 mm bolt circle, centred on the plate

Each corner hole counterbored 10 mm diameter x 4 mm deep from the top

implied: The 31 mm square x 3.4 mm hole pattern and 22.5 mm central bore match a common stepper motor mounting footprint (e.g. NEMA-size motor face), so the plate is sized to accept a motor of that family even though no motor model is named
The boss height and fillet suggest it acts as a spigot/register that locates or clears the motor's front face or pilot diameter, inferred from its position directly around the central bore

The six-hole 56 mm bolt circle and four 5.5 mm corner holes (with counterbores) are fixing points for attaching the plate itself to a larger assembly, inferred from their being separate from the motor pattern and sized for larger fasteners
Counterbores "from the top" imply fastener heads must sit flush or recessed on the top face, inferred from the stated depth and the chamfered top edge treatment

The two slots, described only by position and size, are presumed to be fixing/adjustment or cable-pass features rather than purely decorative, inferred from their size being consistent with M5-class hardware or cable clearance
Choice of PLA and 3D printing implies layered, anisotropic construction with associated strength and heat limitations, inferred from the stated manufacturing process
unstated: Identity/model of the stepper motor (NEMA size, shaft diameter, pilot-boss diameter) that the 31 mm pattern, 22.5 mm bore and boss are meant to mate with
Whether the 22.5 mm bore is a clearance bore for a motor shaft, a spigot/pilot fit for the motor housing, or both, and the required fit/tolerance
Fastener sizes/types intended for each hole set (3.4 mm, 4.5 mm, 5.5 mm) and whether any holes are to be tapped or are plain clearance
Tolerances on all hole diameters, bolt-circle/pattern dimensions, and overall plate dimensions
What the six-hole 56 mm bolt circle and four corner holes attach to (frame, enclosure, another plate) and what fastener/torque loads they will see
Angular start/orientation of the six equally-spaced holes on the 56 mm bolt circle
Purpose of the two 20 x 5 mm slots (adjustment travel, cable pass-through, tie-down) and which hardware passes through them
Surface finish, print orientation, infill percentage, or any other print-quality requirements affecting strength or dimensional accuracy
Operating environment: ambient and motor-generated temperature, humidity, exposure to vibration, duty cycle
Any load the motor itself imposes on the plate during operation (torque reaction, vibration, weight) despite the brief's claim that the part "carries no load"
Required stiffness, flatness, or deflection limits for the mounting face
Overall mass or size constraints of the assembly this plate fits into
Any regulatory, safety, or certification requirements for the equipment this plate is part of
out_of_scope: Specifying load magnitudes, safety factors, or a load case, since the brief states none exists and no figures were given
Selecting a specific motor model or fastener grade
Choosing material grade, infill, or print settings beyond "PLA, 3D-printed" as stated
Determining fits/tolerances not specified in the brief
Assessing or certifying the part for any regulated or safety-critical use
risk_signals: Brief explicitly asserts "it carries no load, so there is no load case" for a plate mounting a motor — this is a stated assumption rather than a derived or verified fact; stepper motors typically impart torque reaction, vibration, and heat even in "no external load" service, and no data is given to confirm these are negligible here

Part is adjacent to an electric motor (heat and vibration source) while being made of PLA, a material with low heat-deflection temperature and creep susceptibility, and no thermal operating range is stated

Part is a mechanical fixture within a motorized/moving assembly, so failure (e.g. boss or counterbore cracking, slot tear-out) could release a rotating motor or allow misalignment, though no information on the larger machine or whether people are near it is given

assumptions.statement: The 3.4 mm, 4.5 mm and 5.5 mm holes are plain through clearance holes (not tapped), matching standard ISO metric clearance drill sizes for M3, M4 and M5 fasteners respectively.
assumptions.rationale: The stated diameters exactly match conventional clearance-hole tables for M3/M4/M5 screws, and nothing in the brief suggests threading.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If any hole is meant to be tapped or sized for a different fastener, the hole diameter and any thread callout would need to change, and hardware chosen against this assumption would not fit.

assumptions.statement: The 22.5 mm central bore is a plain through clearance bore for the motor's spigot/shaft, not a tight precision register fit.
assumptions.rationale: The part is a 3D-printed PLA plate with no tolerance class stated; a clearance bore is the ordinary choice absent a stated fit.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a precision spigot fit was intended, the printed bore (subject to FDM tolerance) may be too loose or too tight for the motor's locating boss.

assumptions.statement: All stated dimensions are held to ordinary FDM 3D-printing tolerance (approximately +/-0.2 mm), with no tighter tolerance called out anywhere in the brief.
assumptions.rationale: No tolerance class is given and the part is explicitly 3D-printed PLA.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Hole and pattern fits with purchased hardware (screws, motor) could be tighter or looser than expected.

assumptions.statement: The six equally-spaced holes on the 56 mm bolt circle may be placed starting at any angular orientation (e.g. symmetric about the plate's length or width axis); no specific clocking relative to the plate or motor pattern is required.
assumptions.rationale: The brief specifies equal spacing and a centred bolt circle but gives no starting angle or alignment to another feature.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a particular clocking (e.g. aligned with corner holes or plate edges) was intended, the as-built orientation might clash with an external fixture, though hole function is unaffected.

assumptions.statement: The plate operates in an ordinary ambient indoor environment, and heat conducted from the mounted stepper motor does not raise the boss or plate above PLA's safe service temperature (roughly 50 degC); no active cooling or thermal isolation is provided.
assumptions.rationale: No operating temperature, motor duty cycle, or thermal management is stated, and PLA has a low heat-deflection temperature.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Sustained motor heat near or above PLA's glass transition could cause the boss or bore to soften, creep or warp over time, degrading the motor's alignment and fit.
